title: An inertia-free Deligne--Mumford stack equals its coarse scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack over $S$ and let $c:\mathcal X\to h_C$ be a coarse moduli morphism to an $S$-scheme $C$, with the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. In particular, for every algebraic space $Z/S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], composition with $c$ is a bijection between $S$-maps $C\to Z$ and maps $\mathcal X\to Z$ up to 2-isomorphism. Suppose every object of $\mathcal X(\Omega)$ has trivial automorphism group for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and every $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$. Then $c$ is an equivalence of categories fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$. Consequently $C$ represents the full groupoid $\mathcal X$, and for every $S$-scheme $T$ each object of $\mathcal X(T)$ has only the identity automorphism, including when $T$ is nonreduced. If $\mathcal X$ is smooth and of finite type over $S$, where smoothness and local finite type are tested on smooth scheme atlases and finite type includes quasi-compactness, then $C\to S$ is smooth and of finite type [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 04SZ, proposition-algebraic-stack-no-automorphisms, with the Deligne--Mumford geometric-inertia criterion of lem-sfb-dm-geometric-inertia-trivial and the coarse universal property. Returned proof Step 4 after the geometric curve calculation and Step 5. The factorization/inverse equations and atlas argument are retained verbatim in report.md; this universal-property consequence is agent-written.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dm-geometric-inertia-trivial]: the hypotheses are exactly that $\mathcal X/S$ is Deligne--Mumford and every object over every algebraically closed $S$-field has trivial automorphisms. Obtain an algebraic space $E/S$ and an equivalence $e:\mathcal X\simeq h_E$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$.

source.place: Tag 04SZ, proposition-algebraic-stack-no-automorphisms; geometric-inertia corollary stated in the cited node

proof.text: Use the coarse universal property [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] with target $E$. It gives $a:C\to E$ with $h_a c\cong e$. Choose a quasi-inverse $d:h_E\to\mathcal X$ and put $b=cd:h_E\to h_C$. Maps of algebraic spaces are natural transformations [def-trf-algebraic-space], so $b:E\to C$ is such a map. Then $ab=\mathrm{id}_E$, since $h_a cd\cong ed\cong\mathrm{id}_{h_E}$ and the target is discrete. Also $(ba)c\cong b e\cong c$. Injectivity of the same coarse universal property, now with target the algebraic space $h_C$ [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], gives $ba=\mathrm{id}_C$. Thus $b$ is an isomorphism and $c\cong h_b e$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Agent universal-property argument after Tag 04SZ; coarse convention in def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids

proof.text: For each $T/S$, the equivalence $c_T:\mathcal X(T)\simeq h_C(T)$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective. The groupoid $h_C(T)$ is discrete by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], so full faithfulness identifies each automorphism set with the singleton identity set. This proves the full-groupoid representability and the assertion for all $T$, without any reducedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 04SZ and the definition of representation by h_C

proof.text: Assume now $\mathcal X/S$ smooth and of finite type. The assumed smoothness, tested on smooth scheme atlases, gives a smooth surjective scheme atlas $a:V\to\mathcal X$ with $V\to S$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: if the test is read as a condition on every smooth scheme atlas, take for $V$ an etale scheme atlas of the Deligne--Mumford stack [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], which is smooth because etale morphisms representable by algebraic spaces are smooth [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Put $q=ca:V\to h_C$, a scheme map $q:V\to C$. For a scheme $T\to C$, the corresponding object of $\mathcal X(T)$ given by the equivalence $c$ identifies the 2-fibre product $V\times_{\mathcal X}T$ with $V\times_CT$; for $T=C$ this is $q$ itself. Since smoothness and surjectivity of $a$ are tested after such scheme base changes, $q$ is smooth and surjective, hence flat and locally of finite presentation [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] to $q$ and the structure map $C\to S$: the composite $V\to C\to S$ is the smooth map $V\to S$, so $C\to S$ is smooth.

source.place: Tag 05B5 (smooth descends along flat surjective lfp maps) as stated in lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent; stack smooth-atlas convention in stacks-morphisms.tex definition-smooth with Tag 06FM, lemma-local-source-target

proof.text: For finite type, [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus] identifies the stack locally-finite-type and finite-type notions with the ordinary algebraic-space notions when the morphism is representable. Here $\mathcal X\to S$ is represented by $C\to S$ via $c$. In particular quasi-compactness is retained, not inferred from local finite type: the affine scheme tests are the same base changes under this equivalence. Hence $C\to S$ is locally of finite type and quasi-compact, which is finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].
